plants.note: Broad leaves come up before the trees leaf out and are gone by early summer; a patch takes years to build.
Three pristine white petals fade to soft pink before summer dormancy claims the forest floor.
Pea blossoms burst straight out of bare dark wood before the heart-shaped leaves unfurl.
White star blossoms open as shad run up the rivers; dark purple berries ripen by midsummer.
Short trellised vines of small plump pods, shelled for very small sweet peas rather than eaten whole.
An old June-bearing berry, small and dark red, soft and very sweet; it bears one heavy crop and is gone.
Silver-grey aromatic foliage and dense purple spires; loves gravelly soil and baking sun.
Blue flowers in a mist of threadlike leaves, followed by inflated horned seed capsules. A spring and early-summer annual.
Crumpled silver-grey and smoky lavender petals around dark stamens; hairy stems and nodding buds. An annual Shirley poppy.
Stout prickly cones ringed by swept-back magenta rays; feeds native bees and winter goldfinches.
Blazing fiery orange flat-topped clusters; essential host plant for monarch butterfly caterpillars.
Shaggy lavender-pink tubular crowns aromatic with oregano-thyme oils; bumblebees crowd the heads.
Deep red-brown blooms that read nearly black in shade, on a compact plant that stays put in a pot.
Potato-leaf Amish heirloom; legendary luscious pink beefsteaks balance deep sweetness and rich acidity.
White heather-bells give way to sweet powder-blue berries; fiery scarlet autumn foliage.
Glossy puckered leaves on stems of red, gold and pink; cut the outer ones and it keeps going until hard frost.
A dwarf sunflower with fully double golden pompom flowers and no dark centre, soft and round like a dandelion clock.
Radiant golden-orange daisies with dark chocolate central cones; long-lasting backbone of the summer border.
Vivid royal purple rays with golden centers celebrate the autumn equinox until heavy frost.
Velvet-furred twigs hold crimson fruit cones through the winter; the long compound leaves go scarlet in fall.
Big golden quinces that scent a whole room; hard and sour raw, they are cooked into paste and jelly.
Classic round heirloom pie pumpkin with dense sweet fine-grained flesh; trailing vines ramble across the garden.
A fat pale root grown in the cool end of the year; cut across, the flesh is magenta inside a green rim.
Leaves come three ways on one tree, plain, mitten and three-lobed; fall runs orange through scarlet.
